MAJOR: `record()` now calls `price_usage()` inline in the event dict; unguarded `int()`/`float()` coercion on provider-supplied token/cost fields raises on malformed values (e.g. `"10.5"`, `"1,000"`, non-numeric cost) and aborts the append-only trail write. Needs safe coercion or a try/except fallback to `cost_source=invalid_usage`/`unavailable`.

The language-rule `allow` exception for `core/execution_trail.py` is granted by the same change that exercises it; the ADR documents it, but this weakens the fail-closed intent of the Go-first rule — the exception should be approved/recorded independently of the change that consumes it, not self-granted inline.

`textwrap.wrap(..., replace_whitespace=False)` preserves embedded `\n`/`\t` in summaries and test commands, which will break box borders and column alignment in `show` output (evidence rendering integrity). Sanitize or normalize whitespace before wrapping.
MINOR: `test_show_renders_stages_tests_and_next` was weakened from structural assertions to substring checks (`"gate0" in out`); a regression back to Markdown tables or broken wrapping would still pass. Same for `test_box_table_wraps_long_cells` (`out.count("|") > 4`).

`_PRICING_CACHE` is process-global with no reload/TTL/invalidation; long-lived gate processes keep stale prices indefinitely. The ADR acknowledges drift but ships no refresh or staleness signal (`fetched_at` is never surfaced in `show` or warnings).

`usage_totals` re-prices every historical event on each `show` while `record` already prices at write time — redundant double computation and mixed-vintage pricing for pre-existing trail files, with no indication of which pricing vintage produced a number.

`price_usage` overwrites `u["model"]` with the normalized name, destroying the original provider model string in the stored evidence (provenance loss); it is also only set on the priced path, not on provider/unavailable paths — inconsistent mutation.
Invalid-usage detection runs after the unknown-model check, so malformed usage for an unrecognized model is reported as `unavailable` rather than `invalid_usage`, masking the data-quality signal.
Validation order means provider-reported cost bypasses the `cached > input` sanity check entirely; fine per precedence, but should be an explicit documented decision, not incidental.
NIT: `_box` computes `top`, `sep`, `bot` as three identical strings; Cursor-style tables normally distinguish the header separator — dead triplication.
Widths use `len()` (character count), not display width; CJK/wide characters in summaries will misalign columns.
`model-pricing.json` `allow` entry is a bare `model-pricing.json` glob that matches any path suffix; a scoped path is more precise for the registry invariant.
Provider cost key probing (`cost`/`total_cost`/`cost_usd`) in `architect_review` is implicit magic; document the expected provider schema.
SUMMARY: Solid change overall: pricing catalog is registered with source/provenance, cost precedence is correct, and the Python exception is durably justified via ADR-0010 with the `edit_growth` allowlist loading bug properly fixed in `change_policy`.

Top risks: unguarded numeric coercion can break trail writes on malformed provider usage (append-only evidence loss), box rendering breaks on embedded whitespace, and the show-rendering tests were weakened below what the acceptance criteria imply.
The language-rule exception being self-granted in-change and the absence of any pricing staleness handling are the principal long-term governance/maintainability concerns.
